messages:
anita: Heads up — onboarding ORBIS-7B (converted from Llama) shows a weird tokenization mismatch when we enable casefold during conversion. Outputs degrade on capitalized acronyms and mixed-case proper nouns. e.g. 'NASA' ends up split oddly. Anyone seen this?

mike: Can you drop a tiny repro + vocab diff? :eyes:

anita: Quick repro below, ran conversion with our standard script and `--casefold True`. Small snippets: 
```bash
# conversion command
python tools/convert_model.py --src=llama/orbis-7b --dst=gemma/orbis-7b --casefold True --out=converted/
```
Diff of tokenization examples (original vs converted):
```
original: "NASA" -> ['N', 'ASA'] (token ids: 345, 12)
converted: "NASA" -> ['Ġnasa'] (token ids: 9012)
original: "HTTP" -> ['H','TT','P']
converted: "HTTP" -> ['Ġhttp']
original: "McDonald" -> ['Mc', 'Donald']
converted: "McDonald" -> ['Ġmcdonald']
```
Also quick eval on wikitext-subset: ppl before conversion=12.3, after conversion+casefold=14.8 (single-run).

kai: Ran a quantized int4 pass on the converted model (hf int4 with qlinear). Numbers look worse: ppl ~16.2 on same slice. So casefold mismatch + int4 appears additive.

sarah: Sounds like conversion is lowercasing/normalizing too aggressively then merging BPE merges that used to keep acronyms as separate subtokens. Our pipeline does `unicodedata.normalize('NFKC')` + `.lower()` when casefold True. That can collapse bytepair boundaries. Try rerunning with casefold disabled or with a two-pass merge that preserves acronym tokens.

anita: Quick test: reran with `--casefold False` and keep original merges, ppl=12.5 — back near baseline. So workaround works but we lose the normalization step clients sometimes expect for user text.

mike: Can we instead special-case tokens that are all-caps in the source vocab and keep them verbatim during conversion? Add an entry in the converter to mark tokens matching `^[A-Z0-9_]{2,}$` as protected, skip lowercasing for those ids.

sarah: That seems reasonable. Also add a small unit check: compare tokenization of 50 common acronyms pre/post conversion and assert token ids map 1:1 or map to a single canonical token.

anita: Will implement. Plan: add `preserve_acronyms=True` flag, run conversion, and re-run our QA eval harness. Adding ticket INFR-1234 to track.

convert-bot: CI: conversion-smoke for model/orbis-7b FAILED — vocab mismatch detected (diff size=34). See logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/convert/4447778888/log

kai: I can prioritize a small quantized rerun once we have a conversion that preserves acronyms. Could we also try int8 calibration sweep to see if quant noise was amplifying the tokenization issue?

mike: Yep. Add `quant-calibration` step to the onboarding checklist and gate int4 perf comparisons until conversion smoke passes.

anita: Note: adding a line to the onboarding doc about casefolding caveats and an example command that preserves acronyms. Will push a draft PR tonight. :thumbsup:

sarah: :thumbsup: Thanks — this explains the odd degradation we saw on enterprise docs with lots of product names.

anita: Filing PR + CI changes now, will ping when green.
